arxiv-2503-00134.creator: Zhongqi Yang, Amir M. Rahmani
arxiv-2503-00134.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) effectively leverage common sense knowledge for general reasoning, yet they struggle with personalized reasoning when tasked with interpreting multifactor personal data. arxiv-2511-18798.title: On the Stability of Discrete Reaction-Diffusion System of Networked Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2511-18798.creator: Dinesh Kumar
arxiv-2511-18798.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dinesh Kumar. Paper provides a sufficient condition for the local stability of the reaction-diffusion system of networked dynamical systems at its homogeneous equilibrium point. It is illustrated through an ecological meta-populations (spatial-structured populations) network of predator-prey systems. Keywords: Reaction-Diffusion System; Metapopulations; Equilibrium Stability; Laplacian Matrix

Introduction

Reaction-diffusion system models arise in many fields of science and support various natural and physical phenomena.

arxiv-2512-08532.title: A Lie-theoretic generalization of some Hilbert schemes
arxiv-2512-08532.creator: Oscar Kivinen
arxiv-2512-08532.description: Abstract . We define several versions of a class of varieties X 𝔤 X_{\mathfrak{g}} attached to a complex reductive Lie algebra 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} , generalizing the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. These include trigonometric and elliptic versions attached to the corresponding groups. We also define the corresponding isospectral varieties Y 𝔤 Y_{\mathfrak{g}} .

arxiv-2601-02090.title: Flo: A data-driven limited-area storm surge model
arxiv-2601-02090.creator: Nils Melsom Kristensen, Mateusz Matuszak, Paulina Tedesco, Ina Kristine Berentsen Kullmann, Johannes Röhrs
arxiv-2601-02090.description: Abstract We present Flo , a data-driven storm surge model, covering the North Sea, Norwegian Sea and Barents Sea. The model is built using the Anemoi framework for creating machine learning weather forecasting systems, developed by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and partners.

pmc-10626747.creator: Junyu Lin, Ruwei Ou, Chunyu Li, Yanbing Hou, Lingyu Zhang, Qianqian Wei, Dejiang Pang, Kuncheng Liu, Qirui Jiang, Tianmi Yang, Yi Xiao, Bi Zhao, Xueping Chen, Wei Song, Jing Yang, Ying Wu, Huifang Shang
pmc-10626747.description: BackgroundReactive astrogliosis has been demonstrated to have a role in Parkinson’s disease (PD); however, astrocyte-specific plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP)’s correlation with PD progression remains unknown. We aimed to determine whether plasma GFAP can monitor and predict PD progression.

pmc-11411126.title: Manipulating conductivity and noise for transitioning between stochastic and inverse stochastic resonances in liquid–crystal electroconvection
pmc-11411126.creator: Jong-Hoon Huh, Takumu Higashi, Yuki Sato
pmc-11411126.description: Noise can play a constructive role in nature and various engineering systems. Over the past four decades, noise-induced stochastic resonances (SRs) have been extensively documented, showing enhancement in system performance. Additionally, inverse SR has been observed in various systems. Typically, these resonances were studied independently.

pmc-11531505.title: Longitudinal genomics reveals carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii population changes with emergence of highly resistant ST164 clone
pmc-11531505.creator: Haiyang Liu, Robert A. Moran, Emma L. Doughty, Xiaoting Hua, Ann E. Snaith, Linghong Zhang, Xiangping Chen, Feng Guo, Willem van Schaik, Alan McNally, Yunsong Yu
pmc-11531505.description: Carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is a persistent nosocomial pathogen that poses a significant threat to global public health, particularly in intensive care units (ICUs). Here we report a three-month longitudinal genomic surveillance study conducted in a Hangzhou ICU in 2021.

pmc-12750772.title: Effects of planting density and foliar fertilization on the phyllosphere microbial community of dual-purpose soybean
pmc-12750772.creator: Qingbiao Xu, Mingyue Huang, Qingfu Huang, Ping Xiong, Mengnan Lu, Caihuan Deng, Qiongmei Song, Yuanyan Meng, Dan Wu, Liuxing Xu
pmc-12750772.description: Soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) is a dual-purpose crop (grain and forage) with considerable economic and nutritional value in modern agriculture. Despite extensive research on soybean cultivation, the synergistic effects of planting density and foliar fertilization on the phyllosphere microbial community structure and its functional diversity remain poorly understood, particularly in dual-purpose soybean production.

pmc-13495582.title: Validation of automated script-based proton therapy optimisation for comparative head and neck planning
pmc-13495582.creator: Marte Kåstad Høiskar, Ulrik Vindelev Elstrøm, Peter Sandegaard Skyt, Kathrine Røe Redalen, Sigrun Saur Almberg
pmc-13495582.description: Background and purposeProton and photon plan comparison is often the gateway to proton therapy for head and neck cancer (HNC). Manual planning is resource demanding, whereas automated planning may efficiently create consistent treatment plans. An automated rule-based intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) plan optimisation script was developed within a commercial treatment planning system for comparative planning.

pmc-13582156.title: Health Literacy in Latin America and the Caribbean: A Comprehensive Scoping Review of Research Developments
pmc-13582156.creator: Kristine Sørensen, Lilliana Villa-Vélez, Stefanie Harsch, Virginia Visconde Brasil
pmc-13582156.description: Health literacy is critical for reducing inequality and promoting effective implementation of health services and better health outcomes. The health literacy agenda is gaining momentum worldwide, including in Latin America and the Caribbean. However, a comprehensive overview of research developments in the region is lacking.

pmc-13694132.title: A Tale of Two Countries: Challenges in the Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging in India and Singapore
pmc-13694132.creator: Charlene Jin Yee Liew, Swati Goyal
pmc-13694132.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This commentary discusses the perspectives of two authors working in India and Singapore in medical imaging and highlights differences in their basic structural and regulatory frameworks. Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) has been established as a trailblazing technology in health care and medical imaging, with the ability to support diagnostic accuracy at high speed, handle high workloads, optimize workflows, and scale imaging expertise even in underserved settings.
